import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffPerPiece
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZar
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarPointwise

/-!
# The widened `DivFamZar` (R2, human decision I-0492)

The endpoint of the widening.  `IsLocallyCertifiedAff` is the locally-certified predicate
whose local certificates are carried by **arbitrary affine-open covers** rather than by basic
opens of a fixed pair of pinned `P¹` charts, and `DivFamZarAff` is its `DivEq` quotient —
the object the human decision of 2026-07-28 is about.

## Why this is strictly weaker than the old predicate, which is the whole point

`FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` (`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean`) turns every old cover datum into
a widened one, and `DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean` migrates the CERTIFICATE on top of it, so
`isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified` holds: anything the old
predicate certified, the new one certifies.  The converse fails, and its failure is exactly
the content of R2 — a divisor straddling both pinned vertical fibres has no chart-typed
certificate (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 4 §4.3, on-stratum witness at every `g ≥ 2`)
but does admit an affine-open one, because `supp D` is finite over `R` and therefore lies in a
single affine open of `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks `0B8B`).

So `DivFamZarAff` is the value on which the divisor functor can be a Zariski sheaf over an
ARBITRARY field, with no `|P¹(k)| ≥ n + 2` hypothesis anywhere — the field-uniform fix.

## The two relocated obligations (I-0492 clause 4)

* **(i) fibrewise-finite support.** NOT a field of anything here.  It is not implied by
  what a `LocalEquations` carries (`d.eqn ≡ r` for a non-unit `r ∈ R` is germ-regular with a
  whole fibre curve in its support), so it must come from the seed's own degree data.  It
  enters as an explicit hypothesis at the point of use, never as carrier data: concretely as
  the `hfib` argument of `AffAdaptation.isCertified_of_swallowedBy`
  (`DivisorFamilyAffAssemble.lean`) and as `AffCoverData.SwallowedBy`
  (`DivisorFamilyAffSwallow.lean`).  Neither is a field of anything in this file.
* **(ii) what the fixed-pair confinement was silently supplying.** Discharged in
  `DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean` (`exists_mem_pieces` from the joint cover,
  `flat_sections_pieces` from the flat structure morphism) and in
  `DivisorFamilyAffPerPiece.lean` (the whole per-piece layer, from openness and affineness).

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff` — a certified family over a widened cover.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyCertifiedAff` — the widened locally-certified predicate.
* `IsLocallyCertifiedAff.of_divEq` — it respects divisor equality.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff` — the widened functor value, with `mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`
  and `picClass`.

The comparison with the chart-typed predicate — `isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified`
and `DivFamZar.toAff` — is in `DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean`, which imports this file.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the pointwise gate,
  one base point at a time, over the widened predicate.
-/

129	
130	`FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` (`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean`) already migrates the COVER

136	relabelled index; the glued clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) transport along `LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft`
137	in its `symm` direction, which evaluates cast-free, so the intertwining with

141	A predecessor docstring here estimated that transport at about a hundred lines of equalizer

160	certified systems of degree `n` up to divisor equality, where "certified" is now witnessed by
161	arbitrary affine-open covers of the relative curve.

154	variable (C π) in
155	/-- **The shifted-datum presentation hypothesis** — the one link of the CHART-U(b) route of
156	record that is not landed, stated exactly.
157	
158	Over an affine test `Spec A`, for a class `μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)` (in practice the
159	twisted family `chartTwist C m Z _ λ` restricted to the test), a presentation is a
160	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `A` whose fibre witness predicate at every residue field agrees
161	with the split witness predicate of `μ` at the corresponding point.
162	
163	Two remarks on the shape, both deliberate:
164	
165	* it is stated as an **agreement of predicates at every point**, not as a class equality.
166	  That is weaker than "the datum's class is `μ`", and it is all the openness argument
167	  consumes — which matters, because the class equality is what needs `cechPicClass_inv` and
168	  a class-level identification, whereas a lane that can produce the pointwise agreement by any
169	  other route may use this theorem immediately;
170	* the split predicate is read at `Over.testPoint`, i.e. at the canonical residue-field point
171	  of the affine test, so no choice of affine chart enters;
172	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` / `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
173	  datum predicate needs are the **canonical** ones of `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`.  An
174	  earlier draft of this file carried them as explicit `alg`/`tow` arguments; that was strictly
175	  worse — it made the statement false for some regradings (`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` reads its
176	  `Algebra` instance inside `relCurveMap`, so a non-canonical `alg` names a different set) as
177	  well as unusable. -/
178	def IsChartDatumPresentation {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) : Prop :=
180	  ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
181	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
182	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)

184	/-! ## The carrier translation: `testPointField` on `Spec A` versus `Ideal.ResidueField`
185	
186	The engine's open set lives in `PrimeSpectrum A` and is indexed by `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`;
187	`chartLocus` lives in `(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and is indexed by `Over.testPointField`.
188	The two carriers are the same space, but the two *fields* are only canonically isomorphic
189	(mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso`), so the witness predicate has to be carried across that
190	isomorphism.  That is what this section does, and it is the transport the (b-amendment) folds
191	into "affine pieces glue by (V1c)-style locality". -/
192	
193	/-- **The residue-field comparison at a point of an affine test, as an algebra map.**
194	
195	`Over.testPointField t` is the *scheme* residue field `(Spec A).residueField t`, while every
196	engine-facing predicate reads the *algebraic* residue field `t.asIdeal.ResidueField` of the
197	prime.  Mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them; this records the identification in
198	the form the tower needs, namely that the canonical `A`-algebra structure on the scheme
199	residue field (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) factors through the algebraic one.
200	
201	Proof: both sides are `Spec.preimage` of a morphism out of `Spec κ(t)`, and `Spec.map` is
202	injective on homs, so it suffices to compare after applying `Spec.map` — where the identity is
203	mathlib's `Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField`. -/
204	lemma algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
205	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
206	    algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
207	      = ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.comp
208	          (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
209	  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
210	  have h : Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)
211	      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField)
212	          ≫ (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv := by
213	    apply Spec.map_injective
214	    rw [Spec.map_preimage, Spec.map_comp]
215	    exact (Scheme.Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField (.of A) t).symm
216	  rw [h]
217	  rfl
218	
219	/-- **The witness predicate at a scheme-residue field agrees with the one at the prime's
220	residue field, and the resulting locus is open.**
221	
222	`Over.testPointField t` is `(Spec A).residueField t` and the engine reads
223	`t.asIdeal.ResidueField`; `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them, and the witness predicate
224	transfers along any field extension in the `A`-tower
225	(`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:142`), in
226	particular along an isomorphism.
227	
228	Three points about the proof, each of which was a suspected wall and is not:
229	
230	* the **carrier identification** `↥(overSpec k A).left = PrimeSpectrum A` is *definitional*
231	  (`Scheme.Spec`'s carrier is `PrimeSpectrum` on the nose), so the two index sets need no
232	  transport and the two topologies agree by `rfl`.  The set equality below is therefore a
233	  pointwise `Iff`, not a homeomorphism argument;
234	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` and `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
235	  predicate needs are **already canonical** (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`,
236	  `Over.instIsScalarTowerTestPointFieldAffine`), so nothing has to be passed in as an
237	  argument.  An earlier draft of this file took `alg`/`tow` as explicit hypotheses and left
238	  the conclusion as a `sorry`; that was a statement-shape artifact, not a gap — and worse,
239	  the hypothesis form is *false for some regradings*, since an arbitrary `alg` need not be the
240	  canonical instance and the predicate is not invariant under regrading the field over `A`;
241	* the only genuine content is the transport across `Spec.residueFieldIso`, which is
242	  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` applied to the isomorphism, in the tower
243	  `A → κ(q) → (Spec A).residueField t` supplied by
244	  `algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors`. -/
245	theorem isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField
246	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
247	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) :
248	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
249	      D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} := by
250	  -- The two loci are the SAME set of the SAME type: `↥(overSpec k A).left` is
251	  -- `PrimeSpectrum A` definitionally, so only the fibre field differs, and the predicate is
252	  -- invariant under the isomorphism between the two readings of it.
253	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
254	        D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)}
255	      = {q : PrimeSpectrum A |
256	          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
257	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
258	                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
259	                    D.cechPicClass
260	              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
261	                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
262	                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
263	    refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
264	    -- the comparison iso as an algebra structure, and its tower over `A`
265	    letI : Algebra (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
266	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
267	      ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.toAlgebra
268	    haveI : IsScalarTower A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
269	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
270	      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors t)
271	    exact (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
272	      (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
273	      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)).symm
274	  rw [hset]
275	  exact D.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ

278	
279	/-- **`chartLocus` over an affine test is the witness locus of a presenting datum.**
280	
281	This is transport (0) (the class-indexation, landed as `cechWitnessLocus`) composed with
282	transport (iii) (locality on the affine test, here trivial because the test *is* affine),
283	run against the presentation hypothesis.  The content is entirely the translation between
284	the two ways the tree indexes a fibre — by a point of the test object's space
285	(`Over.testPoint`, the `chartLocus` side) and by a prime of the test algebra
286	(`q.asIdeal.ResidueField`, the engine side).
287	
288	The translation is available precisely because `Over.testPointField` at a point of
289	`(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and `q.asIdeal.ResidueField` at the corresponding prime are
290	the same field up to the canonical `Spec.residueFieldIso`, and the witness predicate is
291	invariant under field isomorphism over the base (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`
292	applied to an isomorphism). -/
293	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing
294	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
295	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
296	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
297	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
298	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
299	  (hpres t).symm

306	
307	The proof is the route of record with the one missing link supplied as `hpres`: rewrite
308	membership of `chartLocus` as the datum's witness predicate at the residue field of the

310	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` — itself the engine
311	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` read through the GAP-6 dictionary.

313	The general-test statement follows from this one by the affine-piece locality of the
314	(b-amendment)'s transport (iii): `chartLocus` over `T` meets each affine open `U ⊆ T.left` in
315	`chartLocus` over `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` (by `picEtMap_chartTwist` along

318	mathematics; it is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis

321	theorem isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
322	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
323	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
324	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) :
325	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
326	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)} := by
327	  -- The engine's open set is indexed by primes of `A`; the locus is indexed by points of
328	  -- `Spec A`.  These carriers are the same type, so the presentation rewrites one into the
329	  -- other pointwise.
330	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
331	        IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)}
332	      = {t : (overSpec k A).left |
333	          D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} :=
334	    Set.ext fun t => mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing hpres t
335	  rw [hset]

11	# CHART-U(a): `chartLocus`, the chart-membership locus over a general test
12	
13	The co-signed brick of `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3 (CHART-U(a)) and
14	`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6, in the SPLIT form the (a-amendment) binds:
15	
16	> `t ∈ chartLocus c λ` iff for some (equivalently every) finite separable `L/κ(t)`
17	> splitting the collapsed plus class, the honest `L`-class of `λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)` admits
18	> an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`.
19	
20	Everything here is over a GENERAL test `T` and an ARBITRARY plus class
21	`λ ∈ pic0Subgroup C T`.  That is what distinguishes it from
22	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusClass.lean`'s `cechWitnessLocus`, which lives over an affine base
23	and reads an UNTWISTED `CechPic` class; the module header there says so, and this file is
24	the promised general-test article.
25	
26	## The layering, and why the split predicate is a *definition* here and not a disjunction
27	
28	Three separate things had to be joined, and they are joined in three steps:
29	
30	1. `Over.testPoint` (`Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`) turns a point `t : T.left` into a
31	   field point `overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ T`, so that `picEtMap C (testPoint t) λ` is the fibre
32	   class of `λ` at `t`.  Without it there is no way to even state the predicate over a
33	   general test.
34	2. `IsSplitWitness` reads a plus class over a FIELD.  A plus class over a field is
35	   `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`, which is *not* an honest Čech class; the
36	   (a-amendment)'s "finite separable `L` splitting the class" is exactly
37	   `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom` (`Algebra/EtaleCover.lean:287`)
38	   applied to `E`, after which `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_relPicMk_of_algHom`
39	   (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:101`) presents the class as `relPicMk` of an honest
40	   Čech class over `C_L`.  The predicate is then the tree's witness predicate on that Čech
41	   class.
42	3. `chartLocus` twists by the chart index `(m, Σ)` — the same twist
43	   `abelDiv · sigmaFamily Σ · (θ^m)⁻¹` that `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`)
44	   applies on the divisor side — and reads step 2 at step 1's field point.
45	
46	The "some (equivalently every)" of the amendment is the honest content: the ∃-form is what
47	one *proves* (coverage produces one splitting, §1.2 step 6), the ∀-form is what one
48	*consumes* (any presenting splitting is a sound test).  Their agreement is
49	`isSplitWitness_iff_forall`, and it rests on
50	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable`
51	(`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:157`) — the separable-invariance that lane co-owned
52	— together with class-intrinsicity at a fixed field
53	(`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`, `:177`).  So the definition is stated in
54	the ∃-form and the ∀-form is a theorem, not a second definition.
55	
56	## Main declarations
57	
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSplitWitness C π μ` — the split witness predicate at a class
59	  `μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)` over a field `K`: some finite separable `L/K` presents `μ`
60	  as an honest Čech class over `C_L` admitting an effective witness divisor with vanishing
61	  `H¹`.
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_iff_forall` — the (a-amendment)'s "some (equivalently
63	  every)".
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartTwist C m Σ λ` — the twisted fibre family
65	  `λ · sigmaFamily Σ · (θ^m)⁻¹`, i.e. the class whose chart-membership is at issue.  Its
66	  fibre degree is `m·d₁ − Σ.deg` by the landed degree ledger, which the chart-index
67	  constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − g` makes `+g` — the degree at which an effective witness with
68	  `h¹ = 0` can exist at all.
69	* **`AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocus`** — CHART-U(a): `{t : T.left | IsSplitWitness of the
70	  twisted fibre class at κ(t)}`.

72	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocus_preimage_subset` — the naturality half that CHART-U(b)
73	  transport (i) consumes: a morphism of tests pulls `chartLocus` back into `chartLocus`.

113	/-- **The split witness predicate** (CHART-U(a) in the `w4-datb` §1.6 (a-amendment)
114	spelling), at a plus class `μ` over a field `K`.
115	
116	A plus class over a field need not be an honest Čech class — it is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for
117	an étale cover `E` of `K`.  The amendment's "for some finite separable `L/κ(t)` splitting
118	the collapsed plus class" is this: there is a finite separable extension `L/K` over which
119	`μ` becomes `relPicMk` of an honest Čech class `M` on `C_L`, and `M` admits an effective
120	witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`.
121	
122	Stated with the witness clause on a *presenting Čech class* rather than on a datum,
123	because the datum layer is where the shifted-datum constructor (DAT-C GAP-1) is missing;
124	the two agree through `Pic0ChartLocusClass.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.

126	## A convention this predicate INHERITS, and which a consumer must not misread
127	
128	The worksheets say "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`".  The witness clause here —
129	and the tree's `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`
130	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`) that it mirrors, and the GAP-6 dictionary
131	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (`DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:182`) that both rest
132	on — asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  It asks only for a `CurveDivisor` in the
133	class with vanishing `H¹`.  That is deliberate on the tree's side: the dictionary is an *iff*
134	against the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗ L)`, and that
135	condition cannot see effectivity or degree, so adding either clause would break the iff and
136	with it the openness route.
137	
138	Two consequences, both load-bearing:
139	
140	* the degree is supplied **externally**, by the chart-index constraint through
141	  `degAt_chartTwist` below: on a degree-zero `λ` the twisted class has fibre degree
142	  `m·d₁ − deg Z`, which the constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − g` makes `+g`.  It is *not* a
143	  hypothesis of this predicate.  (Until 2026-07-28 this read `−g`, and that sign made the
144	  locus empty for every `g ≥ 1` — see `degAt_chartTwist` and issue I-0514;
145	  `chartTwist_chartValue` now pins the direction by the kernel);
146	* effectivity likewise is not asserted here.  Where the *worksheet's* stronger reading is
147	  actually needed — the canonical-section normalization `h⁰ = 1`, and GAP-2 uniqueness
148	  (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`, which does take `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`) — the
149	  effectivity must be re-supplied at that point.  A lane that reads `IsSplitWitness` as
150	  already giving it will have a gap where it least expects one. -/
151	def IsSplitWitness {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
152	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) : Prop :=
153	  ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
154	      (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
155	      (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic),
156	    PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
157	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
158	      ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
159	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
160	            ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
161	                ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)
162	
163	/-! ## The twisted fibre family -/
164	
165	variable (C) in
166	/-- **The twisted family whose chart-membership `chartLocus` tests**: the plus class `λ`
167	shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family.
168	
169	This is the *class-side* half of `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`): where
170	`chartValue` twists the Abel class of a divisor family, `chartTwist` twists an arbitrary
171	plus class by the same two factors.  A point of `chartLocus` is precisely a point at which
172	`chartTwist` is realised by an effective divisor with no `H¹` — i.e. at which `λ` itself is
173	a chart value, after undoing the twist. -/
174	def chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : picEt C T :=
176	  lam * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m) * (sigmaFamily C Z T)⁻¹
177	
178	/-- **The degree ledger of the twist**: at every field point the twisted family has fibre
179	degree `m·d₁ − deg Z` when `λ` is degree-zero.  With the chart-index constraint
180	`deg Z = m·d₁ − g` this is `+g`, which is the degree at which an effective witness with
181	`h¹ = 0` can exist at all.
182	
183	**Sign discipline, and it was wrong here until 2026-07-28 (issue I-0514).**  `chartTwist`
184	must be the INVERSE of `chartValue`'s twist, not the same one.  `chartValue` is
185	`abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`), so recovering the Abel class from a chart
186	value means multiplying by `θᵐ` and dividing by `Σ` — hence `chartTwist` is
187	`λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`.  An earlier version applied the `chartValue` twist itself, giving fibre degree
188	`deg Z − m·d₁ = −g`; since `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))` forces `deg W ≥ g − 1`, that locus was
189	**empty for every `g ≥ 1`** and its openness was the openness of `∅`.  The comparison point is
190	`degAt_chartValue` at `n = g` (where the chart index is calibrated and `chartValue` lands in
191	`pic0`), NOT at `n = 0`.
192	
193	**An independent confirmation that `+g` is the right target**, worth recording because the
194	wrong sign survived two sessions: at `deg W = g` the rank anchor
195	`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives, for a
196	witness with `h¹ = 0`,
197	`h⁰ = deg W + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1` — exactly the `h⁰ = 1` normalization that DAT-C §2 and
198	GAP-2's uniqueness both require.  So `+g` is not merely the sign that makes the locus nonempty;
199	it is the unique degree at which the witness is *unique*, which is what the chart map needs to be
200	injective.  At `−g` the same anchor gives `h⁰ = 1 − 2g`, negative for `g ≥ 1` — the contradiction
201	that made the locus empty. -/
202	theorem degAt_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
203	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T)
204	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
205	    degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
206	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
207	  rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
208	    degAt_sigmaFamily, (mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hlam) K t]
209	  ring
210	
211	/-- **`chartTwist` inverts `chartValue`'s twist** — the sign check, as a theorem rather than a
212	docstring claim.
213	
214	Applying `chartTwist` to a chart value returns the Abel class it came from.  This is the
215	statement that was FALSE of the earlier definition (which returned
216	`abelDiv · Σ² · (θᵐ)⁻²`), and it is why the direction is now pinned by the kernel: any future
217	edit to `chartTwist` that breaks the inversion breaks this lemma.
218	
219	Recorded per issue I-0514.  A degree ledger alone does not catch a sign error — the wrong-signed
220	ledger was internally consistent — but an inversion law does. -/
221	theorem chartTwist_chartValue {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ)
222	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
223	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
224	    chartTwist C m Z T (chartValue C π n m Z T s) = abelDiv C π n T s := by
225	  rw [chartTwist, chartValue]
226	  group

228	/-! ## CHART-U(a): the locus -/
229	
230	variable (C) in
231	/-- **CHART-U(a), `chartLocus`** (`w4-datc` §3.3, co-signed `w4-datb` §1.6): the set of
232	points of a general test `T` at which the twisted fibre class `λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)` has, after
233	some finite separable splitting of the collapsed plus class at `κ(t)`, an effective witness
234	divisor with vanishing `H¹`.
235	
236	The three layers, each supplied by a named brick:
237	* the *point-to-field-point* passage is `Over.testPoint` (input 0 of this brick — the one
238	  nothing in the tree had);
239	* the *twist* is `chartTwist`, the class-side avatar of `chartValue`;
240	* the *split witness reading over a field* is `IsSplitWitness`.
241	
242	This is the RESERVED name of `Pic0ChartLocusClass.lean`'s header, now defined.  Note it is
243	strictly stronger than `cechWitnessLocus`: general test, twisted class, split predicate. -/
244	def chartLocus (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
245	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) : Set T.left :=
246	  {t : T.left | IsSplitWitness C
247	    (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam))}
248	
249	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
250	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left) :
251	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam ↔ IsSplitWitness C
252	      (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)) :=
253	  Iff.rfl
254	
255	/-! ## The datum-layer reading
256	
257	The witness clause of `IsSplitWitness` is stated on a presenting Čech class over `C_L`.
258	The tree's *engine-facing* predicate is stated on a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum`
259	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`), and
260	the two are joined by `exists_cechPicClass_eq` (every class is presented) plus
261	class-intrinsicity.  This is the seam CHART-U(b) crosses to reach
262	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, so it is recorded here as a lemma of the definition
263	rather than left implicit in the openness proof. -/
264	
265	/-- **The witness clause at a splitting field, in datum form**: for a Čech class `M` over
266	`C_L`, admitting an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹` is exactly
267	`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` of any datum presenting `M` — as a class over the base `L` itself,
268	where `relCurveMap C L L` is the identity comparison.
269	
270	Note the datum lives over the *field* `L` as base ring, which is the affine base the
271	engine's `PrimeSpectrum L` has a unique point of; that is why the fibre reading and the
272	base reading coincide here. -/
273	theorem exists_witness_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_datum
274	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
275	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C L π) {M : (relCurve C L).CechPic}
276	    (hD : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass
277	      = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M) :
278	    (∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
279	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M
280	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
281	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1))
282	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := by
283	  rw [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing, hD]
284	
285	/-- **Upward closure of the witness clause along a separable extension of the splitting
286	field** — the substantive half of the (a-amendment)'s "some (equivalently every)".
287	
288	If a Čech class `M` over `C_L` has an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`, then
289	so does its base change to any finite separable `L'/L`.  This is what makes two splittings
290	of the same plus class comparable: pass to a common separable extension and compare there,
291	rather than comparing the two splittings directly.
292	
293	Proof: present `M` by a datum `D` over `L` (`exists_cechPicClass_eq`); the witness clause at
294	`L` is `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L`, which transfers to `L'` by the co-owned separable
295	invariance `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable`
296	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:157` — itself resting only on faithful flatness of a field
297	extension, so separability is packaging, not content). -/
298	theorem exists_witness_of_separable_extension (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
299	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
300	    {L' : Type u} [Field L'] [Algebra k L'] [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower k L L']
301	    [Algebra.IsSeparable L L'] (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
302	    (h : ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
303	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
304	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
305	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
306	    ∃ W' : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left).CurveDivisor,
307	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L' W' = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L') M
308	        ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
309	            ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left.divisorSheaf L' W') 1) := by
310	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (B := L) (π := π) M
311	  obtain ⟨W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
312	  -- the witness clause at `L` is the datum predicate at `L`: `relCurveMap C L L` acts as
313	  -- the identity comparison on classes, since it is `Spec` of the identity algebra map.
314	  have hid : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass := by
315	    have : relCurveMap C L L = 𝟙 (relCurve C L) := by
316	      rw [relCurveMap]
317	      have hom : overSpecMap (k := k) L L = 𝟙 (overSpec k L) :=
318	        Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simp)
319	      rw [hom, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id]
320	      rfl
321	    rw [this, Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
322	    rfl
323	  have hL : D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := ⟨W, by rw [hid, hD, hW], hW1⟩
324	  -- transfer along the separable extension, then read it back as a witness clause
325	  obtain ⟨W', hW', hW1'⟩ :=
326	    (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable L L').mp hL
327	  exact ⟨W', by rw [hW', hD], hW1'⟩
328	
329	/-! ## Naturality — the half CHART-U(b) transport (i) consumes -/
330	
331	/-- **`chartLocus` is compatible with restriction of the class**: the twist commutes with
332	`picEtMap`, so restricting `λ` along a morphism of tests restricts the twisted family too.
333	
334	This is `sigmaFamily_natural` + `thetaFamily_natural` and nothing else; it is stated
335	separately because transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6 (the descent-preimage step) is exactly
336	this identity read at the field point of a point over the source. -/
337	theorem picEtMap_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
338	    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) :
339	    picEtMap C f (chartTwist C m Z T lam)
340	      = chartTwist C m Z T' (picEtMap C f lam) := by
341	  rw [chartTwist, chartTwist, map_mul, map_inv, map_mul, map_pow,
342	    sigmaFamily_natural, thetaFamily_natural]
343	
344	/-- **`chartLocus` pulls back into `chartLocus`** — transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6, in the
345	form the assembly consumes.
346	
347	For `f : T' ⟶ T` and `t : T'.left`, membership of `t` in the pulled-back locus and of `f t`
348	in the original are the *same* condition on the *same* twisted class, read at two fields:
349	`κ(t)` and `κ(f t)`, with `κ(f t) → κ(t)` the induced extension (`testPointFieldMap`).  So
350	the transport is exactly the invariance of `IsSplitWitness` under that extension.
351	
352	**This lemma proves nothing on its own — it is an interface, and its proof is `hinv`.**  Said
353	plainly so that no lane cites it as if transport (i) were discharged.  What it *does* is fix
354	the exact shape of the obligation and put the burden where it belongs: on the morphism `f`,
355	via the field extension `κ(f t) → κ(t)` it induces, rather than hidden inside the locus.  The
356	tree's landed invariance (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable`) discharges `hinv` when
357	that extension is separable — which is the étale-carrier case the (b-amendment) needs, and is
358	*not* automatic for an arbitrary morphism of tests.  The residue between the two is why
359	`hinv` is a hypothesis and not a `rw`. -/
360	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_mem_chartLocus_comp (m : ℕ)
361	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
362	    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t : T'.left)
363	    (hinv : IsSplitWitness C
364	        (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)) (chartTwist C m Z T lam))
365	      → IsSplitWitness C
366	        (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T' (picEtMap C f lam)))) :
367	    f.left.base t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam
368	      → t ∈ chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C f lam) :=
369	  hinv
370	
371	end

8	/-!
9	# CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST: `isOpen_chartLocus`, and the advertised lemma that did not exist
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean` proves `isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` over an
12	**affine** test, and its docstring says the general-test statement "follows from this one by the
13	affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s transport (iii) … needs no new mathematics".  That
14	claim is right, and this file discharges it — but two of its ingredients were not where the tree
15	said they were.
16	
17	## The advertised lemma that was absent
18	
19	`Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`'s header says chart-independence of the residue field is free
20	"and the chart comparison becomes a lemma (`testPointField_affineOpen_iso`) instead of a side
21	condition.  That is the whole reason this file is short."  **No declaration of that name exists
22	anywhere in the workspace** — the only occurrence was that sentence (cf. I-0624:
23	advertised-but-absent).  Since it is cited as the reason a side condition is unnecessary, it is
24	load-bearing prose, so it is supplied here as `testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso`.
25	
26	It is genuinely cheap, but not for the reason the header gives: what makes it work is that
27	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U` is an **open immersion** on carriers
28	(`IsAffineOpen.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec`), and mathlib already knows the residue-field map of an
29	open immersion is an isomorphism
30	(`Scheme.instIsIsoCommRingCatResidueFieldMapOfIsOpenImmersion`).  So the comparison is an
31	iso for a structural reason, not by a computation with `Spec.residueFieldIso`.
32	
33	## Locality: what "open in every affine piece" needs
34	
35	`isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open`-style bookkeeping is not quite enough, because the locus over the
36	piece is a subset of a *different* space (`Spec Γ(T.left, U)`, not `T.left`).  The bridge is that
37	`fromSpecAffine`'s carrier map is an open immersion with range `U`, so the image of the piece's
38	locus is the intersection of `chartLocus` with `U` — that is what
39	`chartLocus_inter_affineOpen_eq_image` records, and the openness statement then follows from
40	openness of an open immersion's image.
41	
42	## Main declarations
43	
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso` — **the absent advertised lemma**:
45	  the residue-field comparison along an affine-open test object is an isomorphism.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff` — hence the split-witness predicate
47	  at a point of an affine piece agrees with the one at its image in `T`; this is transport (i)'s
48	  hypothesis `hinv` **discharged** for the affine-piece maps (both directions), rather than
49	  assumed.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` — **CHART-U(b) at a general test**: if
51	  `chartLocus` is open over each affine-open test object, it is open over `T`.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_presentations` — the same fed with the per-piece
53	  presentation hypotheses, i.e. the general-test keystone of dat-b row B-4 modulo exactly the
54	  per-piece shifted-datum presentations and nothing else.
55	-/

105	/-! ## Transport (i) for the affine-piece maps, both directions -/
106	
107	variable (C) in
108	/-- **The residue-field-iso invariance of the split-witness predicate** — the obligation the
109	general-test assembly actually rests on, named rather than hidden.
110	
111	`mem_chartLocus_of_mem_chartLocus_comp` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:360`) says transport (i) "proves
112	nothing on its own — it is an interface, and its proof is `hinv`", and that the tree's landed
113	invariance discharges `hinv` for *separable* residue-field extensions.  For an affine-open test
114	object the extension is an **isomorphism** (`Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso` — hence in
115	particular separable), so morally transport (i) is free here.
116	
117	**But the landed invariance is about `HasWitnessH1Vanishing`, not about `IsSplitWitness`**, and no
118	declaration in the tree transports `IsSplitWitness` along a field isomorphism: measured, the only
119	mentions of `IsSplitWitness` invariance are two docstring sentences.  So the affine-piece case of
120	transport (i) needs *one* lemma the tree does not have, which is this predicate.  That is a
121	correction to `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s claim that the general-test statement "needs no new
122	mathematics": it needs exactly this, and nothing else.
123	
124	Why it is believable and small: `IsSplitWitness C μ` is an existential over a finite separable
125	`L/K` presenting `μ`.  Along an isomorphism `K ≃ K'` the same `L` presents the transported class,
126	because `PicEtAff.map` composes (`PicEtAff.map_map`) and the inverse iso undoes the transport —
127	i.e. it is `map_map` plus `map_id`, not geometry.  It is stated as a class-free hypothesis here so
128	that the assembly below is usable the moment a lane proves it. -/
129	def IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant : Prop :=
130	  ∀ (T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))) (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left)
131	    (_ : IsIso (Over.testPointFieldMap f t)) (mu : picEt C T),
132	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (picEtMap C f mu))
133	        ↔ IsSplitWitness C
134	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)) mu)
135	
136	variable (C) in
137	/-- **The split-witness predicate agrees along an affine-open test object**, given the
138	iso-invariance.
139	
140	This is transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6 for the affine-piece maps, in **both** directions — so
141	the locus over the piece and the locus over `T` correspond exactly, which is what the locality
142	assembly needs (a one-sided containment would not give openness).
143	
144	The only input beyond landed material is `hinv`; the `IsIso` it is applied at is discharged by
145	`Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso`, i.e. structurally, by mathlib's fact that an open
146	immersion induces an isomorphism of residue fields. -/
147	theorem isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
148	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) (mu : picEt C T)
149	    (t : (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)).left) :
150	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t)
151	        (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) mu))
152	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C
153	          (Over.testPoint (T := T) ((Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base t)) mu) :=
154	  hinv T (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) t
155	    (Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso T U t) mu
156	
157	/-! ## Locality: the general-test assembly -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **The affine piece's locus is the preimage of the general-test locus.**
161	
162	For an affine open `U ⊆ T.left`, `chartLocus` over the affine test object `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` is
163	the preimage, along the carrier map of `Over.fromSpecAffine T U`, of `chartLocus` over `T`.
164	
165	Both sides unfold to the same split-witness condition read at two residue fields, so this is
166	`isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff` applied pointwise together with `picEtMap_chartTwist` (the
167	twist commutes with restriction). -/
168	theorem chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
169	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
170	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) (lam : picEt C T) :
171	    chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)
172	      = (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base ⁻¹' chartLocus C m Z lam := by
173	  refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
174	  rw [Set.mem_preimage, mem_chartLocus_iff, mem_chartLocus_iff,
175	    ← picEtMap_chartTwist]
176	  exact isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff C hinv T U (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
177	
178	variable (C) in
179	/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST**, i.e. the statement `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring
180	promises follows from the affine case "by the affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s
181	transport (iii)".
182	
183	If `chartLocus` is open over every affine-open test object of `T`, it is open over `T`.
184	
185	The bookkeeping is genuinely bookkeeping — but note *which* bookkeeping, because it is not the
186	`isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter` the docstring names: the piece's locus lives in a **different
187	space** (`Spec Γ(T.left, U)`, not `T.left`), so the bridge is that the carrier map is an open
188	immersion whose range is `U` (`IsAffineOpen.range_fromSpec`).  The preimage identity
189	`chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage` then turns per-piece openness into openness of
190	`chartLocus ∩ U`, and the affine opens cover `T.left`. -/
191	theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
192	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
193	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
194	    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
195	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :
196	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z lam) := by
197	  -- Openness is local: it suffices that every point of the locus has an open neighbourhood
198	  -- inside it, and each point lies in some affine open of `T.left`.
199	  rw [isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open]
200	  intro t ht
201	  -- an affine open around `t`
202	  obtain ⟨U, hUmem⟩ : ∃ U : T.left.affineOpens, t ∈ U.1 := by
203	    obtain ⟨U, hU, hmem, -⟩ :=
204	      (TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp T.left.isBasis_affineOpens)
205	        (show t ∈ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) from trivial)
206	    exact ⟨⟨U, hU⟩, hmem⟩
207	  -- the piece's locus is open, and its image is `chartLocus ∩ U`
208	  have hpre := chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage C hinv m Z T U lam
209	  refine ⟨chartLocus C m Z lam ∩ U.1, Set.inter_subset_left, ?_, ht, hUmem⟩
210	  -- `chartLocus ∩ U` is the image of the piece's locus under an open immersion with range `U`
211	  have hoi : IsOpenImmersion (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left := U.2.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec
212	  have hrange : Set.range (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base = (U.1 : Set T.left) := by
213	    change Set.range (U.2.fromSpec).base = _
214	    exact U.2.range_fromSpec
215	  have himg : (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base ''
216	        (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))
217	      = chartLocus C m Z lam ∩ U.1 := by
218	    rw [hpre, Set.image_preimage_eq_inter_range, hrange]
219	  rw [← himg]
220	  haveI := hoi
221	  exact (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.isOpenEmbedding.isOpenMap _ (haff U)
222	
223	end

9	/-!
10	# `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` DISCHARGED — CHART-U(b) at a general test, unconditionally
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusGeneralTest.lean` proves CHART-U(b) over a general test *modulo one
13	hypothesis*: `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C`, the transport of `IsSplitWitness` along an
14	**isomorphism** of reading fields.  That was the single input standing between the landed
15	affine openness and `isOpen_chartLocus` over a general test, and its own docstring priced it as
16	"`PicEtAff.map_map` plus `map_id`, not geometry".
17	
18	**This file proves it, and the price was almost that.**  The route is:
19	
20	1. the residue-field extension a morphism of tests induces is a `k`-algebra map
21	   (`Over.testPointFieldMap_comp_algebraMap`) — this was *not* recorded anywhere, and it is what
22	   lets the extension be read as an `AlgHom`/`AlgEquiv` at all.  It is `Spec.preimage` applied to
23	   the naturality square `Over.testPoint_comp_left`, plus the two `Over` triangles;
24	2. an invertible extension is therefore a `k`-algebra **equivalence**
25	   (`Over.testPointFieldAlgEquiv`);
26	3. `IsSplitWitness` is invariant along such an equivalence
27	   (`isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_iff`);
28	4. the naturality square in the `overSpecMap` spelling (`Over.testPoint_comp`) turns (3) into
29	   `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant`.
30	
31	## What step (3) actually costs, and where the prediction was right
32	
33	The prediction was `map_map` + `map_id`; what it *is* is `PicEtAff.map_map` in the
34	`mapAlg`-into-a-common-target form (`PicEtAff.map_mapAlg_eq_map`) plus
35	`picEtAffineEquiv_naturality`, and the witness clause is carried through untouched.  So the class
36	side is indeed pure functoriality.
37	
38	**What the prediction did not mention is the instance side, and that is the real content.**
39	`IsSplitWitness C μ` existentially quantifies a splitting field `L` *together with seven
40	instances*, four of them about `L` over the reading field: `Algebra K L`, `IsScalarTower k K L`,
41	`Module.Finite K L`, `Algebra.IsSeparable K L`.  Transporting the predicate along `e : K ≃ₐ[k] K'`
42	keeps **the same `L`** but must re-derive all four over `K'`, along `e.symm`.  Two of them are
43	mathlib transports found by name (`Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv`,
44	`Algebra.IsSeparable.of_equiv_equiv`, both stated for exactly this square) and two are
45	`IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq`.  A one-line `rw` this is not; but it is bookkeeping, and no
46	geometry enters — in particular nothing about the curve, the twist, or `H¹` is touched.
47	
48	## Why the forward direction genuinely needs an EQUIVALENCE, not an `AlgHom`
49	
50	`isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap` is stated for `e : K ≃ₐ[k] K'` and the `≃` is load-bearing at a
51	precise point: the transported `Algebra K' L` is `algebraMap K L ∘ e.symm`, which needs `e`
52	*surjective*.  Along a non-invertible `K → K'` there is no `K'`-algebra structure on the old `L`
53	at all, and one would have to base-change `L` — which is the separable-extension route
54	(`exists_witness_of_separable_extension`), a different and strictly harder lemma.  So the `IsIso`
55	hypothesis of `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` is not packaging; it is what makes the same `L` work.
56	
57	## Main declarations
58	
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointFieldMap_comp_algebraMap` — the induced residue-field
60	  extension is a `k`-algebra map.
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointFieldAlgHom` / `Over.testPointFieldAlgEquiv` — that extension
62	  as an `AlgHom`, and as an `AlgEquiv` when it is invertible.
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPoint_comp` — the `Pic0ChartTestPoint` naturality square as an
64	  equality of morphisms **in the slice**, through `Over.overSpecMap`.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mapAlg_eq_map` — `map_map` in the form this needs: an explicit
66	  `k`-algebra map into a common target is absorbed by `PicEtAff.map`.
67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_iff` — `IsSplitWitness` is invariant along a
68	  `k`-algebra equivalence of the reading field.
69	* **`AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds`** — the hypothesis of
70	  `Pic0ChartLocusGeneralTest`, discharged.
71	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage'`,
72	  `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` — the general-test statements with the
73	  hypothesis removed.  **`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` is CHART-U(b) at a general test with
74	  no residue**, which is what `c9b` consumes as the `V` of `restrictChart`.
75	-/

95	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
96	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
97	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
98	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

102	namespace Over
103	
104	/-! ## The residue-field extension is a `k`-algebra map
105	
106	`testPointFieldMap` is defined as a bare `CommRingCat` morphism (`Scheme.Hom.residueFieldMap`),
107	and `Pic0ChartTestPoint` records only its `Algebra` reading via `testPointFieldAlgebra`, which
108	makes `κ(t)` a `κ(f t)`-algebra *without* saying anything about `k`.  For the plus-class
109	transport that is not enough: `PicEtAff.mapAlg` consumes a `k`-**algebra** map, so the fact that
110	the extension is one over `k` has to be proved.  It is exactly the two `Over` triangles read
111	through `Spec.preimage`. -/
112	
113	/-- **The residue-field extension induced by a morphism of tests is a `k`-algebra map.**
114	
115	`testPointFieldMap f t : κ(f t) → κ(t)` commutes with the two `k`-algebra structures of
116	`Pic0ChartTestPoint`, both of which are `Spec.preimage` of a composite down to `Spec k`.  The
117	proof is the naturality square `testPoint_comp_left` composed with `T.hom`, pushed through
118	`Spec.preimage` (a bijection on homs out of an affine, so it turns the commuting square of
119	schemes into the commuting square of rings). -/
120	theorem testPointFieldMap_comp_algebraMap {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
121	    (t : T'.left) :
122	    (testPointFieldMap f t).hom.comp
123	        (algebraMap k (testPointField (T := T) (f.left.base t)))
124	      = algebraMap k (testPointField (T := T') t) := by
125	  have hw : (testPoint t).left ≫ T'.hom
126	      = Spec.map (testPointFieldMap f t)
127	          ≫ ((testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)).left ≫ T.hom) := by
128	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← testPoint_comp_left f t, Category.assoc, Over.w f,
129	      Over.w (testPoint t)]
130	  have hpre := congrArg (fun g => (Spec.preimage g).hom) hw
131	  simp only [Spec.preimage_comp, Spec.preimage_map, CommRingCat.hom_comp] at hpre
132	  exact hpre.symm
133	
134	/-- The residue-field extension at a point, as a `k`-algebra map. -/
135	def testPointFieldAlgHom {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left) :
136	    testPointField (T := T) (f.left.base t) →ₐ[k] testPointField (T := T') t :=
137	  { (testPointFieldMap f t).hom with
138	    commutes' := fun r => congrFun (congrArg DFunLike.coe
139	      (testPointFieldMap_comp_algebraMap f t)) r }
140	
141	/-- **An invertible residue-field extension is a `k`-algebra equivalence.**  This is the shape
142	the `IsSplitWitness` transport consumes, and the `IsIso` hypothesis of
143	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` exists precisely to supply it. -/
144	def testPointFieldAlgEquiv {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left)
145	    [IsIso (testPointFieldMap f t)] :
146	    testPointField (T := T) (f.left.base t) ≃ₐ[k] testPointField (T := T') t :=
147	  { (asIso (testPointFieldMap f t)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv with
148	    commutes' := (testPointFieldAlgHom f t).commutes }
149	
150	/-- **The naturality square of the bridge, in the slice.**  `Pic0ChartTestPoint.testPoint_comp_left`
151	states it for the underlying scheme morphisms; every class-level transport needs it for the
152	`Over`-morphisms themselves, since `picEtMap` is indexed by those.  Faithfulness of
153	`Over.forget` (`Over.OverMorphism.ext`) is the whole content. -/
154	theorem testPoint_comp {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left) :
155	    testPoint t ≫ f
156	      = overSpecMap (testPointFieldAlgHom f t) ≫ testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t) :=
157	  Over.OverMorphism.ext (by
158	    rw [Over.comp_left, Over.comp_left, Over.overSpecMap_left]
159	    exact testPoint_comp_left f t)
160	
161	end Over

163	namespace PicEtAff

165	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
166	/-- **`map_map` in the form the transport needs**: an explicit `k`-algebra map `e : K → K'` that
167	is compatible with two towers into a common `L` is absorbed by `PicEtAff.map`.
168	
169	`PicEtAff.map_map` is stated for a chain of `Algebra` instances; here the middle step is an
170	explicit `AlgHom`, so the `Algebra K K'` it needs is manufactured from `e` and the
171	`IsScalarTower K K' L` from `halg`.  This is the class-side half of the whole iso-invariance,
172	and it is pure functoriality — no field, separability or finiteness hypothesis appears. -/
173	theorem map_mapAlg_eq_map {K K' L : Type u} [CommRing K] [Algebra k K]
174	    [CommRing K'] [Algebra k K'] [CommRing L] [Algebra k L]
175	    [Algebra K L] [Algebra K' L] [IsScalarTower k K L] [IsScalarTower k K' L]
176	    (e : K →ₐ[k] K') (halg : ∀ x : K, algebraMap K' L (e x) = algebraMap K L x)
177	    (a : PicEtAff C K) :
178	    PicEtAff.map C L (PicEtAff.mapAlg C e a) = PicEtAff.map C L a :=
179	  letI : Algebra K K' := e.toRingHom.toAlgebra
180	  haveI : IsScalarTower k K K' := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (e.commutes x).symm
181	  haveI : IsScalarTower K K' L := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (halg x).symm
182	  PicEtAff.map_map C K' L a
183	
184	end PicEtAff

186	/-! ## Iso-invariance of the split predicate -/
187	
188	variable (C) in
189	/-- **`IsSplitWitness` transports along a `k`-algebra equivalence of the reading field**
190	(forward direction).
191	
192	The splitting field `L` is **not changed**: along `e : K ≃ₐ[k] K'` the same `L` presents the
193	transported class, via the `K'`-algebra structure `algebraMap K L ∘ e.symm`.  That is where the
194	`≃` is used and cannot be weakened — for a non-invertible `K → K'` no such structure exists and
195	one must base-change `L` instead (`exists_witness_of_separable_extension`, a strictly harder
196	statement).
197	
198	The four instances about `L/K` are re-derived over `K'`: `Algebra K' L` and
199	`IsScalarTower k K' L` by `of_algebraMap_eq`, and `Module.Finite K' L`,
200	`Algebra.IsSeparable K' L` by mathlib's transports along the same commuting square
201	(`Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv`, `Algebra.IsSeparable.of_equiv_equiv`).  The class equation is
202	`picEtAffineEquiv_naturality` plus `PicEtAff.map_mapAlg_eq_map`, and the witness clause `(W, hW,
203	hW1)` is carried through **untouched** — it lives over `L`, which did not move. -/
204	theorem isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap {K K' : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
205	    [Field K'] [Algebra k K'] (e : K ≃ₐ[k] K') (nu : picEt C (overSpec k K))
206	    (h : IsSplitWitness C nu) :
207	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap e.toAlgHom) nu) := by
208	  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hKL, htow, hfin, hsep, M, hM, W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
209	  letI := hLfield
210	  letI := hkL
211	  letI := hKL
212	  haveI := htow
213	  haveI := hfin
214	  haveI := hsep
215	  -- the SAME `L`, now a `K'`-algebra along `e.symm`
216	  letI hK'L : Algebra K' L := ((algebraMap K L).comp e.symm.toRingHom).toAlgebra
217	  have halg : ∀ x : K, algebraMap K' L (e x) = algebraMap K L x := fun x => by
218	    change (algebraMap K L) (e.symm (e x)) = _
219	    rw [e.symm_apply_apply]
220	  haveI htow' : IsScalarTower k K' L := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => by
221	    change algebraMap k L x = (algebraMap K L) (e.symm (algebraMap k K' x))
222	    rw [show e.symm (algebraMap k K' x) = algebraMap k K x from
223	      (e.symm.commutes x).trans rfl, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k K L]
224	  -- the commuting square both mathlib transports are stated against
225	  have hcomp : ((algebraMap K' L).comp (e.toRingEquiv : K →+* K'))
226	      = ((RingEquiv.refl L : L →+* L)).comp (algebraMap K L) :=
227	    RingHom.ext fun x => halg x
228	  haveI hfin' : Module.Finite K' L :=
229	    Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv e.toRingEquiv (RingEquiv.refl L) hcomp
230	  haveI hsep' : Algebra.IsSeparable K' L :=
231	    Algebra.IsSeparable.of_equiv_equiv e.toRingEquiv (RingEquiv.refl L) hcomp
232	  refine isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness C _ M ?_ W hW hW1
233	  rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality, PicEtAff.map_mapAlg_eq_map e.toAlgHom halg]
234	  exact hM
235	
236	variable (C) in
237	/-- **Iso-invariance of `IsSplitWitness`, as an `iff`.**  The reverse direction is the forward
238	one at `e.symm`, since `overSpecMap` is functorial and `e.symm ∘ e = id`.  An `iff` is what the
239	locality assembly needs: a one-sided containment would not give openness. -/
240	theorem isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_iff {K K' : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
241	    [Field K'] [Algebra k K'] (e : K ≃ₐ[k] K') (nu : picEt C (overSpec k K)) :
242	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap e.toAlgHom) nu)
243	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C nu := by
244	  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap C e nu⟩
245	  have hid : Over.overSpecMap (k := k) e.symm.toAlgHom ≫ Over.overSpecMap e.toAlgHom
246	      = 𝟙 (overSpec k K) := by
247	    rw [← Over.overSpecMap_comp, show e.symm.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom = AlgHom.id k K from
248	      AlgHom.ext fun x => e.symm_apply_apply x, Over.overSpecMap_id]
249	  have hback := isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap C e.symm _ h
250	  rwa [← picEtMap_comp, hid, picEtMap_id] at hback
251	
252	variable (C) in
253	/-- **`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` — DISCHARGED.**
254	
255	The hypothesis `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusGeneralTest.lean` carries, and the only input standing
256	between the landed affine openness of `chartLocus` and CHART-U(b) at a general test.  With it,
257	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` below is unconditional.
258	
259	The assembly is the naturality square in the slice (`Over.testPoint_comp`): reading the class at
260	`κ(t)` after restricting along `f` equals restricting along `Spec` of the residue-field
261	extension, which under the `IsIso` hypothesis is `Spec` of a `k`-algebra **equivalence** — and
262	along one of those `IsSplitWitness` is invariant. -/
263	theorem isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C := by
264	  intro T T' f t hiso mu
265	  haveI := hiso
266	  have hfac : picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (picEtMap C f mu)
267	      = picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap (Over.testPointFieldAlgHom f t))
268	          (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)) mu) := by
269	    rw [← picEtMap_comp, ← picEtMap_comp, Over.testPoint_comp f t]
270	  rw [hfac, show Over.testPointFieldAlgHom f t
271	      = (Over.testPointFieldAlgEquiv f t).toAlgHom from AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl]
272	  exact isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_iff C (Over.testPointFieldAlgEquiv f t) _

11	## What this file closes
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece
14	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, and its header says plainly what it does not do:
15	
16	> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
17	> nothing here produces such a datum.
18	
19	**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
20	sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
21	**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
22	`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
23	so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
24	on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
25	`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
26	it they are the same class.
27	
28	## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction
29	
30	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
31	plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
32	plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
33	from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.
34	
35	That restriction is real and is named `IsPlusHonest` below.  It is **not** vacuous and **not**
36	automatic:
37	
38	* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
39	  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
40	  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
41	* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
42	  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
43	  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
44	  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.
45	
46	  **A CORRECTION TO THIS PARAGRAPH, from a fresh-context review of the commit that first wrote
47	  it, and it is the same failure this leaf recorded one round earlier.**  When first committed the
48	  sentence above cited `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` **and that declaration did not exist** — a
49	  workspace-wide grep returned exactly one hit, the sentence itself.  That is precisely the
50	  failure mode r7 diagnosed (`docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`) and filed a lesson about,
51	  reproduced by the very session that filed it, inside its own *non-vacuity* argument.
52	  A kernel check, a `sorry` census and an axiom probe are all silent about it.
53	
54	  It also mattered mathematically, which is why it was worth writing rather than deleting: the
55	  θ- and Σ-witnesses are the **twist factors**, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest` discharges anyway,
56	  so they say nothing about the class being *charted*.  Since `chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`,

58	  carrying the whole of the final clause.  It is now proved (below), so the paragraph stands as
59	  written; had it not been, the honest statement would have been "no residue beyond
60	  `IsPlusHonest lam`", with the Σ-chart clause unproved.

174	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` asks for is met outright, with no choice left to the caller.
175	
176	This is the statement `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean`'s header names as not claimed, and it
177	too is `GeometricallyReduced`-free. -/
178	theorem exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A))
180	    (hμ : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k A), relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) z = μ) :
181	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π, IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D := by
182	  obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := hμ
183	  obtain ⟨L₀, rfl⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k A) z
184	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq
185	    (C := C) (B := A) (π := π) L₀
186	  exact ⟨D, isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt C π L₀ D hD⟩
187	
188	/-! ## The honesty hypothesis, and why it is not vacuous -/
189	
190	variable (C) in
191	/-- **The honesty hypothesis: `μ` is a plus unit on every affine piece of the test.**
192	
193	This is the one thing the producer needs of `μ`, and it is a genuine hypothesis rather than a
194	restatement: a plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`, and
195	`Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is the record that it becomes honest over `E.Carrier` and not over
196	`A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is exactly the gap between an arbitrary class and one the producer reaches.
197	
198	It is stated per affine piece because that is the shape `isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` consumes;
199	over an affine test it is the single condition that `μ` is in the range of `relPicToPicEt`. -/
200	def IsPlusHonest (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (μ : picEt C T) : Prop :=
201	  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)),
202	    relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) z
203	      = picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) μ
204	
205	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] in
206	variable (C) in
207	/-- Honesty is closed under multiplication — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a subgroup, and
208	`picEtMap` is a homomorphism. -/
209	theorem IsPlusHonest.mul {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ ν : picEt C T}
210	    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) (hν : IsPlusHonest C T ν) :
211	    IsPlusHonest C T (μ * ν) := by
212	  intro U
213	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
214	  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hν U
215	  exact ⟨z * w, by rw [map_mul, hz, hw, map_mul]⟩
216	
217	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] in
218	variable (C) in
219	/-- Honesty is closed under inversion. -/
220	theorem IsPlusHonest.inv {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ : picEt C T}
221	    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) :
222	    IsPlusHonest C T μ⁻¹ := by
223	  intro U
224	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
225	  exact ⟨z⁻¹, by rw [map_inv, hz, map_inv]⟩
226	
227	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] in
228	variable (C) in
229	/-- Honesty is closed under powers. -/
230	theorem IsPlusHonest.pow {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ : picEt C T}
231	    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) (m : ℕ) :
232	    IsPlusHonest C T (μ ^ m) := by
233	  intro U
234	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
235	  exact ⟨z ^ m, by rw [map_pow, hz, map_pow]⟩
236	
237	variable (C) in
238	/-- **A θ-family is honest at every test** — the first half of the non-vacuity check.
239	
240	`thetaFamily_natural` restricts a θ-family to a θ-family, and `thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv`
241	says its affine collapse is the plus unit of the base-changed base class.  So a θ-family is in the
242	range of the unit on every affine piece, with no hypothesis on the curve.
243	
244	This is why `chartTwist` preserves honesty: two of its three factors are θ-families. -/
245	theorem thetaFamily_isPlusHonest (L₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic)
246	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
247	    IsPlusHonest C T (thetaFamily C L₀ T) := by
248	  intro U
249	  refine ⟨relPicAlgMap C (Algebra.ofId k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (relPicMk C (overSpec k k) L₀), ?_⟩
250	  rw [thetaFamily_natural]
251	  exact (picEtAffineEquiv C Γ(T.left, U.1)).injective (by
252	    rw [picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt, thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv])
253	
254	variable (C) in
255	/-- A Σ-family is honest: it *is* a θ-family (`sigmaFamily` is defined as one). -/
256	theorem sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
257	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
258	    IsPlusHonest C T (sigmaFamily C Z T) :=
259	  thetaFamily_isPlusHonest C _ T
260	
261	variable (C π) in
262	/-- **THE ABEL VALUE IS HONEST AT EVERY TEST** — the witness that carries weight, and the one this
263	file's header cited by name before it existed (see the header's own retraction).
264	
265	The θ- and Σ-family witnesses above are the *twist factors*, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest`
266	discharges anyway; they say nothing about the class being charted.  Since
267	`chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` and honesty is a subgroup condition, honesty of a **chart
268	value** reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` — so this is the row that makes CHART-U(b) unconditional
269	on the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart actually reads.
270	
271	It is cheap for a structural reason: `abelDiv`'s components are `abelDivPlus`, i.e. `PicEtAff.unit`
272	of `relPicMk` of the family's class, and `relPicToPicEt`'s components are `PicEtAff.unit` of
273	`relPicMap` — so the witness on the piece `U` is the class of the *restricted* family, and
274	`abelDiv_val` plus `picEtMap_abelDiv` line the two up. -/
275	theorem abelDiv_isPlusHonest {n : ℕ} (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
276	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
277	    IsPlusHonest C T (abelDiv C π n T s) := by
278	  intro U
279	  refine ⟨relPicMk C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1))
280	    ((divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n Γ(T.left, U.1)
281	      (divFamZar.map C π n (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) s)).picClass), ?_⟩
282	  rw [picEtMap_abelDiv, abelDiv_overSpec]
283	  rfl
284	
285	variable (C) in
286	/-- **`chartTwist` PRESERVES honesty** — the reason the producer reaches the Σ-chart.
287	
288	`chartTwist λ = λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`, and both twist factors are θ-families, hence honest at every test
289	with no hypothesis.  Since honesty is a subgroup condition, the twisted class is honest exactly
290	when `λ` is.
291	
292	So the residue of CHART-U(b) is **the λ-factor alone**: no twist bookkeeping enters, which is the
293	mis-pricing the §3.3 correction 5 records. -/
294	theorem chartTwist_isPlusHonest (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
295	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
296	    IsPlusHonest C T (chartTwist C m Z T lam) := by
297	  rw [chartTwist]
298	  exact (hlam.mul C ((thetaFamily_isPlusHonest C (thetaCechClass C) T).pow C m)).mul C
299	    ((sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest C Z T).inv C)
300	
301	/-! ## CHART-U(b) with the residue discharged -/
302	
303	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
304	variable (C π) in
305	/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST, WITH NO RESIDUE**, for a class that is honest on the affine
306	pieces of the test.
307	
308	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` needs a per-piece datum with the plus-class property;
309	`exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` produces one from honesty, and
310	`chartTwist_isPlusHonest` says the twist does not disturb honesty.  So the whole chain — the
311	engine, RE-5, the dictionary, the fibre-field invariance, `haff`, the presentation, `hconv`,
312	`hplus`, and now the producer — closes on the single hypothesis `IsPlusHonest`.
313	
314	`IsAffineHom π` follows from `IsFinite π`, whence the disabled overlapping-instance linter — the
315	same configuration `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_plusFibre` carries and for the same reason. -/
316	theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest
317	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
318	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
319	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
320	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z lam) :=
321	  isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre C π hπ m Z T lam fun U =>
322	    exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range C π _
323	      (by
324	        obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := chartTwist_isPlusHonest C m Z T hlam U
325	        exact ⟨z, hz.trans (picEtMap_chartTwist m Z (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)⟩)
326	
327	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
328	variable (C π) in
329	/-- **The chart locus as an OPEN OF THE TEST, from honesty alone** — the shape the `W` field of a
330	chart datum consumes (`chartLocusOpens`, `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:115`), with its `haff`
331	argument discharged rather than passed through.
332	
333	This is c9b's clause (i) paid in full for an honest class: not "reduced to", but produced. -/
334	def chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
335	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
336	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
337	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
338	    T.left.Opens where
339	  carrier := chartLocus C m Z lam
340	  is_open' := isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest C π hπ m Z T lam hlam
341	
342	@[simp]
343	lemma mem_chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
344	    {hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom}
345	    {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
346	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} {hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam}
347	    {t : T.left} :
348	    t ∈ chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest C π hπ m Z T lam hlam ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
349	  Iff.rfl
350	
351	end
352	
353	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise
7	
8	/-!
9	# B-5 at the Abel chart: what the pointwise datum unfolds to, and what it costs
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduces `ChartsCoverLocally` — hence B-6 — to a
12	four-part datum at each point of each test.  That reduction is stated for an *arbitrary*
13	family of presheaf maps, so it says nothing about how hard the datum is at the family that
14	matters.  This file instantiates it at `abelSigmaChart` and computes the answer.
15	
16	## The computation, and the one thing it makes visible
17	
18	A section of `pic0SigmaSheaf C` over a **bare** test scheme `T` is by definition a *pair*
19	`⟨a, λ⟩` with `a : T ⟶ Spec k` and `λ` a degree-zero class on the slice object `Over.mk a`
20	(`Over.sigmaExtension`, `Picard/OverSigmaExtension.lean`).  And `(Over.mk a).left` is `T`
21	itself, definitionally.  So the big-site/slice crossing that looks like it needs a bridge does
22	not: the pointwise datum's `t : ↥T` *is* a point of the slice test, and `chartLocus` applies to
23	it with no transport.  `abelChartApp_eq` below records the crossing as an equation rather than
24	leaving it to unfold at a use site.
25	
26	What the computation *does* make visible is where the cost sits.  `abelSigmaChart`'s value at
27	`x : W ⟶ D.left` is `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv …)⟩`, so matching it against the
28	restriction of `⟨a, λ⟩` needs **both** components: the Σ-component is an equation between
29	morphisms to `Spec k`, and only then is there a class equation.  A producer that supplies the
30	class half alone has not supplied the datum — the Σ-component is what pins the chart point to
31	lie *over* the test, and it is free only because `W.ι ≫ a` is what `D.hom` must equal.
32	
33	## THE CORRECTION THIS FILE CARRIES, against this lane's own headline
34	
35	`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:40` says of its `chartLocusOpens`:
36	
37	> `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised — the `W` field costs zero, which is
38	> a real reduction of the datum from four fields to three
39	
40	**The second clause is false, and the roadmap `c9b` row repeats it** ("`W` needs nothing").
41	`chartLocusOpens` takes an argument `haff`, the affine-local openness of the locus at every
42	affine open of the test, and *nothing in the tree discharges it*:
43	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance.lean`) removed the
44	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis and passes `haff` straight through, as does
45	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it.  The affine case that would feed it is
46	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`), which is
47	itself conditional on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — B-4's *named residue*.
48	
49	**Update, same session** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`): that residue is now
50	*entirely witness-free*.  Its forward half already was (the trivial splitting), and its
51	converse `hconv` — the descent direction, open for three sessions — is discharged by plus-unit
52	injectivity.  So what `haff` ultimately costs is a `cechPicClass` base-change identity: no
53	witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, and nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.
54	
55	So the honest accounting is: **`W` costs `haff`, which costs B-4's presentation residue.**  The
56	datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  What is
57	genuinely free is the type-level crossing above, and `chartLocusHaff` below is the residue
58	named so it cannot be lost again.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelChartApp_eq` — the Abel chart's value at a point of the divisor
63	  scheme, as an explicit `Sigma.mk`.  Both components, since the datum needs both.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartLocusAffineLocal` — the `haff` residue, named.  This is what
65	  `chartLocusOpens` silently costs.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens_of_affineLocal` — `chartLocusOpens` from it, so the
67	  dependency is explicit in the API rather than in an argument position.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation` — the residue **reduced to B-4's
69	  own named obligation**: a per-affine-piece `IsChartDatumPresentation` gives it.  This is the
70	  link that was asserted in `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring and never written.
71	-/

80	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

82	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
83	
84	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
85	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
86	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
87	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
